fund-js/13-async-await-patterns/01-map-w.instructions:
**Skills:** concurrency · Promise.all  
**Level:** ★★★

**Interview prompt.** "We resize 5,000 images with an external API that allows 4 concurrent requests. Write the helper."

**Why it matters.** `Promise.all(items.map(fn))` starts everything at once. A small pool of workers that pull the next item when they finish keeps exactly N calls in flight and still returns results in input order.

**Your task.** Export `mapLimit(items, limit, fn)`. It returns a promise of an array where element i is the result of `await fn(items[i], i)`, and:
- at most `limit` calls of `fn` are in flight at any moment
- results are in INPUT order, whatever order the calls finish in
- if any call rejects, the returned promise rejects with that reason (calls already started may finish, but no NEW call starts after the failure)
- an empty `items` array resolves to `[]`

`limit` is a whole number of 1 or more.

**Worked example.** With items `[30, 10, 20]` (each `fn` waits that many ms and returns it) and limit 2, the result is `[30, 10, 20]`, and never more than 2 calls overlap.
hints: Instead of starting one promise per item, start a few worker loops that each keep taking the next item.

Start a fixed number of worker loops that share one next-index counter, have each store its result at the index it claimed, wait for all the workers, and use a shared failure flag so no new work starts after an error.
Run a fixed number of loops in parallel that each claim the next unclaimed position, store their result at that position, and stop claiming as soon as any call has failed.
